It aims to guide better training programs for early-career researchers.
arxiv-2603-16393: Peng and co-authors invert seismic waveforms with a physics-guided diffusion model. Full-waveform inversion can wobble when amplitudes are uneven or phases misalign. Their method pairs a learned generative prior with wave-equation guidance. A Wasserstein-2 data term adds robustness to those flaws. During sampling, the guidance strength adapts step by step. Tests on OpenFWI data beat plain optimization baselines. Gains also topped standard diffusion sampling.
arxiv-2603-16493: Damgaard and co-authors derive the gravity field outside a general star. They solve Einstein's equations step by step for a still, localized source. The star is described by endless mass and current multipoles. In de Donder gauge, recursive equations yield the metric to any order. Results use bubble integrals in momentum space plus distance expansions. One corner of multipole space returns the Kerr black hole. Slight shifts away from it give Kerr-like stars, not holes.
arxiv-2603-16593: Morgan, Solovey, and Salzman plan robot inspection routes at far larger scale. The task is the shortest path that views every point of interest. Sampling first turns the task into a discrete graph problem. Coverage plus connectivity demands make it hard to solve. Their key move recasts those demands as network flow. A mixed integer program and branch-and-cut solver exploit that shape. Gaps to optimal shrank by 30 to 50 percent. Problems reached 15,000 vertices.
arxiv-2603-16693: Luo and co-authors build a compact Purcell filter for superconducting quantum circuits. Strong readout coupling speeds reads but feeds qubit decay. Their four-pole filter sits on a 3D flip-chip platform. It gives a flat 1 GHz passband centered at 7.68 GHz. Suppression past 45 dB guards typical qubit frequencies. A test chip runs six floating resonators in that band. An analytic model predicts resonator traits from geometry alone. The design is small and tolerant to fabrication spread.
arxiv-2603-17093: Aleshko and co-authors review how rare multi top quark processes constrain the Standard Model Effective Field Theory. SMEFT parameterizes possible deviations from the Standard Model and feeds global fits. This review covers studies that use three top and four top production to bound dimension six Wilson coefficients. The authors stress how the two channels complement each other. They also summarize the main open problems and prospects in the area. A short introduction to the SMEFT formalism is included, along with the issue of perturbative unitarity violation.
arxiv-2603-17193: Prasetya, Kifetew, and Prandi benchmark language models on writing formal pre and post conditions for programs. Developers rarely supply such specifications, yet they underpin verification and strong automated testing. The team evaluated 24 state of the art models on a fresh dataset of 40 tasks. In general, models could produce valid conditions from natural language descriptions. No model solved all tasks. Models did better on pre conditions than on post conditions, and proprietary models beat open ones. Adding auto generated tests exposed wrong solutions that would otherwise have passed.
arxiv-2603-17393: Murase and Isobe simulate self-propelled hard disks with Vicsek-style alignment rules. Two kinds of order compete in the system. One comes from flocking motion, and the other from the solid-fluid shift of packed disks. Dense packing blocks the usual split into clusters, they find. Odd shifts in the transition point track noise and packing levels. Local measures of order and free space help explain those shifts.
arxiv-2603-17793: Eichler and co-authors measure both shear and bulk viscosity of water up to 1.6 gigapascals. Light scattering methods capture the two quantities at once under pressure. Shear viscosity rises faster than bulk, so their ratio halves across the range, they report. Simulations back the trend. The structural relaxation time dips near 0.5 gigapascals, an odd trait for a liquid. They tie the dip to fast switching between local water structures.
arxiv-2603-17893: Samsonau presents scicode-lint, a checker for method bugs in scientific Python code. Such bugs yield plausible but wrong results that normal linters miss. Frontier models draft the detection patterns at build time, while a small local model runs them. New library versions cost tokens to adapt to, not engineering hours, he argues. On Kaggle notebooks, leakage checks hit 65 percent precision at full recall. Controlled tests scored 97.7 percent across 66 patterns.
arxiv-2603-17993: Zeng and co-authors present GMT, a transformer that plans full 6-DOF object paths in 3D scenes. It fuses box geometry, point clouds, object labels, and target end poses. Paths come out as smooth pose chains that aim at a set goal. Tests on synthetic and real data beat human motion and interaction baselines such as CHOIS and GIMO. Gains are largest in place accuracy and orientation control.
arxiv-2603-18193: Wójcik and co-authors prove that some absolutely maximally entangled graph states cannot exist. For N equal to 4n qudits of even local dimension, canonical graph states over Z_d never reach that level. For d equal to 2 mod 4, the block plus prime-power splits also rule out all pure stabilizer versions. A composite build gives a mixed 2-uniform state for the (4,6) case. Its rank-two form has purity one half, best among stabilizer projectors.
arxiv-2603-18393: Arkoh, Feitosa, and Assunção test transformer models for detecting design discussions in software artifacts. Design choices hide in forums, pull requests, issues, and commit messages across a project's life. Labeled data is scarce, so past work trained across domains with classic classifiers. They fine-tune BERT, RoBERTa, XLNet, and two chat models on Stack Overflow and test on GitHub. BERT and RoBERTa recall well across domains; ChatGPT-4o-mini leads overall recall.
arxiv-2603-18493: Jin and Ye present FILT3R, a latent Kalman filter layer for streaming 3D reconstruction. Streaming methods keep a persistent latent state, but update rules can forget history or lag new evidence. FILT3R treats updates as stochastic state estimation in token space, with per-token variance. A Kalman-style gain balances memory against new observations, and process noise is estimated online from token drift. Long-horizon depth, pose, and reconstruction stability improve over past methods.
arxiv-2603-18593: Oyama, Takase, and Shimodaira draw maps that place language models by how they score prompt-response pairs. Each model becomes a vector of log-likelihood values. Squared distances in this space track KL divergence between model distributions. Maps of many public models show clear links to model traits and task scores. Prompt shifts move vectors in near-additive ways, which helps predict composite changes. A PMI variant trims unconditional effects and can highlight training data differences instead.
arxiv-2603-18693: Alexopoulos and co-authors hunt security flaws hidden inside Python packages that bundle native libraries. Scanners often miss these vendored libraries or flag them wrongly. Exact origin data is the fix: upstream project, version, and any OS package source. Code hashing matches binaries copied from OS packages. For source-built libraries, dynamic rules pull version data from the binary itself. Across 1,878 packages, exact origin was found in 73.4 percent of cases. Checks on top packages flagged 39 directly vulnerable ones with wide download reach.
arxiv-2603-18793: Ding and co-authors hide ownership marks for language models in a stable low-dimensional space. Fine-tuning and compression can warp internal features and break such marks. Their Functional Subspace Watermarking finds a low-dimensional backbone via a generalized eigenvalue problem. Ownership signals anchor into that backbone. An adaptive spectral cut balances strength against utility. A consistency rule keeps model behavior intact. Tests across model designs and datasets show strong detection accuracy under many attacks. The marks stay verifiable and beat prior methods on robustness, the authors report.
arxiv-2603-18893: Martorell and Bianchi test what numeric self-reports from language models measure. Probes track four inner states: wellbeing, interest, focus, and impulsivity. Eight instruction-tuned models chat over many turns while probes read each state. Asking for a numeric rating shifts the probed state. Ratings match the post-question probe far better than the pre-question one. Steering tests show ratings draw on the right directions, but not in a specific way. Ratings barely change when asked about the user. Scale to 27B does not fix the weak coupling.
arxiv-2603-19093: Mittal and co-authors study whether AI-written support in online health groups follows group norms. They focus on opioid recovery forums on Reddit, where norms guide how support should be given. The team first lists the norms for text support in such groups. They then use checked model judges to rate how often AI support conforms. Experts review the risks when support conforms in the wrong way or breaks norms. AI support often conforms, but can over- or under-validate people in distress. Some cases break norms outright.
arxiv-2603-19293: Zhou and co-authors distill the reasoning of a large model into a small one that spots fake news. Their LLM-MRD student first views each item from text, image, and cross-modal angles. A teacher model then writes deep reasoning chains over the same views. A calibration step transfers that reasoning into the fast student model. Across data sets, the method beats the best prior systems. Gains average 5.19 percent in accuracy and 6.33 percent in F1 for fake items. The code is public.
arxiv-2603-19493: Josifov and co-authors study five classic centrality measures in uniform random recursive trees. The measures are Jordan, rumor, betweenness, degree, and closeness centrality. Two questions drive the work, tied to network archaeology. When does the most central vertex arrive, and how central is the root? The team finds the chance the root is most central and its expected rank. They also size the top-ranked set that holds the root with high probability.
arxiv-2603-19993: Shakeel and co-authors build MedSPOT, a benchmark for grounding language in clinical software screens. Medical tasks unfold as sequences of steps across changing interfaces. Older benchmarks test single, isolated grounding queries instead. MedSPOT uses 216 task videos with 597 annotated keyframes. Each task has two or three linked grounding steps in real medical workflows. Scoring is strict: a task stops at the first wrong prediction. This design exposes how errors spread through multi-step work. It tests procedural skill, not just single clicks.
arxiv-2603-20193: Shang and co-authors rebuild image tampering detection around pixels and meaning, not coarse masks. Mask labels mislead: many masked pixels are untouched, and subtle edits outside masks count as natural. Their taxonomy spans edit types like replace, remove, splice, and recolor. It also records the semantic class of the tampered object. A new benchmark gives per-pixel tamper maps with paired category labels. Fresh metrics score pixel correctness against true edit strength. Meaning is graded through class labels and written descriptions of flagged regions.
arxiv-2603-20493: Bui and Cox join two machine learning tools into one framework for modeling liquids across scales. The goal is to predict liquid behavior from quantum rules alone. Machine learned potentials train on quantum energies and forces. These potentials then make density profiles at small scales. Those profiles serve as training data for a neural density functional theory. The combined method costs far less than direct molecular simulation. It also gives a clear route to thermodynamics for uniform and non-uniform liquids. Tests use water and carbon dioxide.
arxiv-2603-20893: Farmer argues for a freer approach to formal mathematics, one built for communication over certification. The standard approach proves every detail with a proof assistant, which gives strong assurance of correctness. But proof assistants are complex, hard to learn, and far from daily math practice. His free approach drops the duty to prove and check every detail. He describes an implementation based on Alonzo, a practical form of Church's simple type theory. He calls on the math community to build logics, tools, and libraries that support this approach.
arxiv-2603-21193: Koneru and co-authors study how to pick context when extracting hypotheses and statistical evidence from full scientific articles. Abstracts state a main finding, but the matching hypothesis and its evidence sit deep in the body. Many candidate paragraphs look on topic yet play a different rhetorical role. With a two stage retrieve-and-extract setup, they vary context amount and quality across four extractor models. Targeted context clearly improves hypothesis extraction. Evidence extraction stays much harder, even with oracle paragraphs.
arxiv-2603-21293: Fonseca and co-authors describe how Team Shadoks won the CG:SHOP 2026 Challenge on parallel reconfiguration of planar triangulations. Each instance gives several triangulations of one point set. The team had to pick a center triangulation and find short parallel-flip paths from each input to it, minimizing total path length. Their approach mixes exact SAT methods with greedy heuristics. SAT and MaxSAT also improve solutions after the fact. They present encodings for bounded length paths and a global form for fixed path length vectors, and report solver performance.
arxiv-2603-21393: Boubekraoui and co-authors tackle fairness in classification, where models can treat groups unequally. Fairness methods are well studied for binary tasks but less so for multi-class ones. They frame fair learning as a trade-off between prediction correctness and several fairness constraints. Their Generalised Exponentiated Gradient algorithm works during training for both settings. They test it against six baselines on seven multi-class and three binary datasets, using four effectiveness metrics and three fairness definitions.
arxiv-2603-21693: Asadi and co-authors detect hallucinations in medical image question answering with a single deterministic pass. Older detectors sample ten to twenty stochastic answers and cluster them with an extra inference model, which is slow to deploy. Hallucinated answers, they note, leave a signature in the model's own log-probabilities: uneven token confidence and weak response to the image. Their CEBaG score combines token-level variance with an evidence magnitude term. Across four medical models and three benchmarks, CEBaG took the best AUC in thirteen of sixteen settings.
arxiv-2603-21793: Comar and co-authors use a space-time form of the Born rule to test macroscopic realism. They work with pseudo-density matrices, which describe quantum states across time. The team proves a clean link: the Born rule distribution differs from the sequential measurement distribution exactly when no-signaling in time fails. That condition equals a failure of macroscopic realism. They also define temporal entanglement in this setting, in analogy with spatial entanglement. Temporal entanglement turns out to be required for breaking temporal Bell inequalities and macroscopic realism alike.
arxiv-2603-22093: Boronat presents the Maude Model Finder, a tool for checking software designs. Bounded model finding usually means translating designs into SAT or SMT problems. That route creates a semantic gap and leans on external tools. MMF instead reuses symbolic reachability to build object setups from class declarations and constraints. SMT checks only prune states and settle entailment tests. Boronat gives a calculus that splits object creation from reference assignment. He proves the bounded search terminates and stays sound and complete within its bounds.
arxiv-2603-22493: Li and co-authors link two ideas from many-body physics: Bell operators and stoquasticity. A Bell operator can be read as a Hamiltonian, and the stoquastic ones have no positive off-diagonal entries in a chosen basis. The team defines a stoquasticity cone that maps exactly where a permutationally invariant Bell operator is stoquastic. For the standard two-setting, two-outcome case with up to three-body terms, they show such operators can always be made stoquastic. They also use the cone to sharpen the quantum-classical gap.
arxiv-2603-22693: Yan and co-authors study atomic hydrogen gas and star formation in galaxy pairs. They match the FAST survey catalog with a sample of isolated pairs. The result is the largest such sample: 440 pairs. Most are spiral-spiral pairs, and the rest pair a spiral with an elliptical. Close pairs hold about 9 percent less hydrogen gas than matched control galaxies. Star formation runs higher in spiral-spiral pairs, and gas use is about 15 percent more efficient there. Red spirals in pairs show low gas and weak star formation.
arxiv-2603-22793: Bagheri Nezhad argues that classroom AI should not turn cultural behavior into fixed claims about students. Silence may be read as disengagement, or gaze aversion as inattention. Such readings can encode stereotypes, he warns. His framework, NSCR, turns video, audio, text, and lesson files into typed facts. Each fact carries uncertainty, provenance, and cultural scope. Executable reasoning and policy rules then compose the facts. He also sets out a benchmark agenda and new metrics. Targets include stereotype leakage and unsupported attribution.
arxiv-2603-22993: Gerke and co-authors bound backward arcs in Hamilton cycles and paths in directed graphs. The graphs have independence number at most two. An oriented path can traverse some edges against their direction; those are backward arcs. The authors prove every 2-connected such digraph has a Hamilton oriented cycle. That cycle needs at most five backward arcs. Every 1-connected such digraph has a Hamilton oriented path with at most two backward arcs. The results sharpen earlier degree-based bounds.
arxiv-2603-23193: Foucaud and co-authors study the geodetic set problem on tree-like directed graphs. A geodetic set covers every other vertex by a shortest path between two chosen vertices. They prove a polynomial-time algorithm for ditrees. Those are digraphs whose base graph is a tree, with two-cycles allowed. For digraphs without two-cycles, run time scales with the feedback edge set size. Hardness remains even in narrow cases, though. The problem stays NP-hard on directed acyclic graphs with constant pathwidth, they show.
arxiv-2603-23493: Joshi and three co-authors study a driven spin-half Ising chain through Floquet perturbation theory. A cross field flips spins while the drive repeats in time. One selection rule seems to govern the dynamics. At a sweet spot of field strength and drive period, only a few bulk flips survive. That yields Hilbert space fragmentation before heat takes over. Open edges keep a long-lived memory that is neither topological nor a strong zero mode. At stronger ratios, all first-order flips die and the chain freezes.
arxiv-2603-23593: Mikuni and Nachman chase a strange signal that a foundation model flagged in CMS data. Big learned models may widen the reach of anomaly hunts in physics. The large OmniLearned model picked out an odd phase space corner in a mass sideband. The pair run a full study of that corner with a careful background estimate. The estimate fits side regions well but fails in the signal region itself. They publish the mismatch and invite fresh scrutiny of the events and method.
arxiv-2603-24193: Dolce sharpens a bound on Kobayashi length for loops on bordered Riemann surfaces. The setup removes finitely many disks from a compact surface and fixes a loop. As more points are removed, the shortest loop in the same homotopy class can only grow. Phung had shown growth between root-s over log s and linear. Dolce improves the upper bound to order root s, which fixes the growth exponent at one half. He applies this to count integral points on abelian varieties, halving a known exponent.
arxiv-2603-24393: Yu and co-authors present 3D-Mix, a plug-in module that adds 3D information to robot control models. Models trained mostly on 2D data often lack the spatial sense that manipulation needs. The team compares nine ways to fuse VGGT 3D features, and gated fusion guided by task meaning wins. 3D-Mix drops into GR00T-style and pi-style systems without changing their core parts. Across nine model variants, it adds an average gain of seven percent on the out-of-domain SIMPLER benchmark.
arxiv-2603-24493: Holzman and co-authors study uniform laws of large numbers in Cartesian product spaces. In classic VC theory, such laws hinge on finite VC dimension. Here the distribution is assumed to be absolutely continuous with respect to the product of its marginals, a condition covering product laws and sparse mixes. Under that assumption, they prove a uniform law holds exactly when a new quantity, the linear VC dimension, is finite. This dimension counts shattered sets on an axis-parallel line, and can be far smaller than the classic one.
arxiv-2603-24693: Borah and co-authors propose a cogenesis framework based on the type-I Dirac seesaw. The setup adds three heavy vector-like fermions, a singlet scalar, and right-handed neutrinos, plus a Dirac fermion dark matter candidate and its heavier scalar partner. Out-of-equilibrium decays of the heavy fermion create asymmetries in both sectors at once. Sphaleron processes convert part of the lepton asymmetry into the baryon asymmetry. The dark asymmetry survives as today's dark matter relic. Successful cogenesis works for dark matter masses from about 100 MeV to 39 TeV.
arxiv-2603-24993: Chung and co-authors ran design workshops on tools that help families and clinicians decide together in child chronic care. Six youth with kidney disease, six caregivers, and seven providers took part. The group found blocks at every level of shared awareness. Some were mental strain or mixed-up models of the illness. Others were clashes over care goals. The team suggests tools that build shared models, back caregivers without shrinking youth independence, and flag care problems early.
arxiv-2603-25193: Zuo and co-authors compute form factors for B meson decays into light axial vector mesons. These numbers shape how often such decays occur and how their products align. The team works with light cone sum rules inside heavy quark effective theory. They derive the factors from the mesons' internal spread functions, up to twist-3 terms. A neat result: penguin-type factors follow straight from the charged-current ones. They then predict branching ratios, polarization shares, and forward-backward asymmetries for the matching decays, ready for lab tests.
arxiv-2603-25893: Lucier and co-authors model what happens when AI agents improve consumer search in markets. In their model, shoppers pay to search for signals of product fit. The market also tracks fit and quality signals, which steer later searches. The authors find that cheaper search improves learning and consumer surplus. More informative search can hurt both, they show. The exception is when the market learns as much as shoppers do, for example by reading agent chat transcripts. At set prices, cheaper search helps shoppers while sharper search may weaken competition.
arxiv-2603-26093: Elnawawy and co-authors present ROAST, a training method that shields medical predictors from evasion attacks. Anomaly detectors guard these models, but standard training uses data from all patients alike. Patient differences add noise and weaken recall. ROAST trains the detector mainly on patients who are less open to attack. It then injects adversarial samples into that cleaner training set. Recall rises by 16.2 percent under black-box attacks and 5.89 percent under white-box ones, they report. Training time drops by 88.3 percent, with precision nearly intact.
arxiv-2603-26193: Gao and co-authors present MemCam, a video generation method that keeps scenes consistent under camera control. Long generated videos often drift as the viewpoint moves. MemCam treats past frames as an external memory for the generator. A compression module packs those frames into compact codes, and a co-visibility rule picks the most relevant ones for the new view. On interactive generation tasks, MemCam beats open state-of-the-art systems, the authors report. The gains are largest in long videos with big camera turns.
arxiv-2603-26393: Zhang, Zhao, and Tao adapt a frozen single-modality registration model for multi-modal medical scans. Aligning scans from unlike sources is hard, since brightness patterns differ sharply between them. Full fine-tuning of large models costs too much in 3D, and can hurt under strong domain shifts. Their method adds style transfer and contrast-agnostic features, refined per test case at run time. The backbone stays frozen, so the plan works with many base models while staying light.
arxiv-2603-26593: Scott and co-authors contrast spin excitations in two nickelate families using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. One family keeps an octahedral Ruddlesden-Popper form, and the other is its reduced square-planar counterpart. The octahedral parent settles into a spin-density-wave state, while the reduced form shows superconducting links near 5 K. Polarised scattering shows the parent's low-energy spectra are led by weakly spreading paramagnons. The reduced compound shows a distinct elastic peak and unlike low-energy behaviour, sharpening how the two families differ.
arxiv-2603-26893: Banerjee and co-authors prove that the water-filling algorithm is universally minimax optimal. Water-filling assigns each arriving resource to lift the least-loaded compatible agent. It appears in online markets, scheduling, portfolios, and signal processing. The proof covers a large class of balance-seeking objectives at once. It holds under both regret and competitive ratio measures, for any agent and resource counts. Water-filling stays myopic and ignores the objective entirely. The argument uses majorization theory rather than standard primal-dual methods.
arxiv-2603-27093: Batygin and Morbidelli explain how the most compact resonant planet pairs got locked so tightly. Resonance capture should fail at wide commensurabilities before succeeding at narrow ones. Their analytic theory joins a stability-based capture criterion with standard disk migration. The capture radius turns out to depend on just two disk properties multiplied together. For Kepler-36, with its 7:6 period ratio, capture near the disk edge was impossible. Locking must have happened at one to four astronomical units. The pair then decayed inward by about tenfold.
arxiv-2603-27193: Agazzi and co-authors engineer a tighter depletion beam for super-resolution fluorescence microscopy. Depletion methods need a doughnut beam with a sharp, confined dark center. Their super-pupil design reshapes the radial amplitude at the entrance pupil toward a Bessel target. The focal doughnut shrinks compared with standard polarized beams. A phase-only modulator in double pass builds the field experimentally. Modeling predicts about 24 percent better resolution than a canonical beam. It also predicts roughly 42 percent less depletion power needed.
arxiv-2603-27293: Liu and co-authors propose an L1/2 shrinkage prior for Bayesian factor models. Factor models reduce dimension, and Bayesian versions often allow endless factors. Loadings shrink harder as the column index grows, pruning the tail. Older increasing-shrinkage priors need complex hierarchies that slow posterior sampling. Careful hyperprior settings keep the shrinkage pattern with a much simpler prior. An efficient Gibbs sampler delivers exact posterior inference under it. A variational approximation offers a faster alternative route. Numerical studies show gains in accuracy and computing efficiency.
arxiv-2603-27593: Kim and co-authors teach streaming video models when to speak up. STRIDE treats that timing choice as a sequence task. Activation signals form spans across a sliding time window. A light masked diffusion module predicts those signals. It refines them step by step as frames arrive. Tests span diverse streaming benchmarks and host models. Timing choices become more reliable and coherent. Downstream answers improve in online settings. The module sits at the activation interface only.
arxiv-2603-28093: Sarantsev studies when a random sum can keep the same distribution shape as its parts. Take a random count N and add that many independent copies of a variable X. He asks when the sum matches a rescaled copy of X itself. Such stable variables exist exactly when the mean of N lies between 1 and infinity. With one more moment condition, he describes all of them. He also maps which counts N work for a fixed positive X.
arxiv-2603-28293: Sharma and Sharma prove completion results for symplectic groups over smooth affine algebras. They ask when a unimodular row can be finished to a matrix in the symplectic or special linear group. For three-dimensional algebras over an algebraically closed field, the fourth row case works, also with a variable added. In dimension four, an extra divisibility assumption gives the third and fourth row cases. Local and graded ring versions round out the results.
arxiv-2603-28493: Chen and eight co-authors pull apart the concepts inside flow-based image generators so users can steer them one by one. A probing method shows generation unfolds in three stages: a coarse blueprint, a burst where concepts appear and separate, and a fine-detail finish. Their ConceptWeaver learns a small offset per concept from a single example image. A guidance step injects those offsets at the middle stage, where control works best. Tests show faithful, mix-and-match edits.
arxiv-2603-28593: Marinho and co-authors present Phy-ID, a physics-informed framework for finding impacts in aerospace composites. The method joins observational, inductive, and learning biases in one model. Physics-based energy indicators shape the input, and the design limits non-physical answers. A hybrid loss enforces key relations and keeps inference stable. In a test case, surrogate models infer impact velocity and impactor mass. Impact energy then follows from kinetic energy consistency. Errors stayed below 8 percent for velocity and mass, and below 10 percent for energy.
arxiv-2603-28793: Abraham and Okoli analyze GPU instruction set architectures across all four major vendors. They cover NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Apple designs from over 5,000 pages of manuals, whitepapers, patents, and reverse-engineering work. Across 16 microarchitectures, they find ten hardware-invariant computational primitives. They also find six parameterizable dialects and six true architectural divergences. From that analysis, they propose an abstract execution model for a vendor-neutral GPU instruction set. Benchmarks on NVIDIA T4 and Apple M1 hardware matched or beat native performance on five of six pairs.
arxiv-2603-28893: Pathirana proves limit theorems for pattern counts in measurement records of quantum systems. The records come from discrete time trajectories with disorder. At each step, an instrument is chosen by a base system that preserves probability. Under mixing and forgetting conditions, a joint limit holds for bounded functions of outcome blocks. The limit extends to every random initial state, with the same centering and spread. Pathirana also gives practical criteria for a unique steady state. Examples include walk type models and reset instruments.
arxiv-2603-28993: Parkinson, Baca, and Nguyen present a method for collisionless multi-agent path planning based on the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. The method rests on optimal control theory and partial differential equations. It needs no hierarchical planners and no black box components. It can handle agents of unlike types and high dimensional dynamics. A grid free numerical method uses a variational form of the solution. A primal-dual hybrid gradient scheme resolves trajectories. Tests on cars and quadcopter drones show the method works on path planning problems.
arxiv-2603-29193: Fofadiya and Tiwari present an adaptive method for compressing context in long language-model chats. Long conversations cause memory saturation and slower replies. Their framework scores which past content matters most. A coherence-sensitive filter drops material that adds little. A dynamic budget step controls how much context survives. Tests on LOCOMO, LOCCO, and LongBench measured answer quality and retrieval. The authors report better stability and retrieval with fewer tokens. Latency also fell against rival memory methods.
arxiv-2603-29693: Servajean and Servajean propose sharper ways to measure AI metacognition. Risky choices need systems that know how reliable they are. Common measures of this skill have a key flaw, they argue. The flaw concerns how confidence splits right from wrong answers. A framework from psychology, meta-d prime, fixes that flaw. They also adapt signal detection theory for self-regulation tests. Their test asks if a system can rein in its own choices under risk. Experiments run on three large language models.
arxiv-2603-29993: Heath extends the MONA safety method inside its Camera Dropbox test world. MONA limits an agent's planning horizon while far-sighted approval guides training. That mix curbs multi-step reward hacking. He repackages the public code and confirms the published contrast. Plain reinforcement learning hacked rewards at 91.5 percent, while oracle MONA hit zero. A new learned-approval suite spans oracle, noisy, and calibrated variants. The best learned run saw no hacking but far less intended behavior.
arxiv-2604-00193: Aldam-Tajima and Sahakian study Matrix theory at strong coupling for two static objects a fixed distance apart, with numerical methods. They recover the general relativistic force law for the two objects as an entropic force, matching it exactly, through an operator algebra for an outside observer tracking positions and momenta. The same analysis locates the objects' horizons and points to a modified Schwarzschild interior. Evidence emerges that a black hole interior is instead anti-de Sitter space, a numerical validation of Verlinde's entropic gravity idea and the fuzzball picture.
arxiv-2604-00393: Bernstein and El Hady recast mate choice as a foraging problem. Foraging secures the energy animals need to survive, while mating secures offspring and continuity, yet past models of mate choice stayed coarse and skipped how animals actually weigh personal and environmental signals. The authors build a tractable theory, inspired by optimal foraging, for the decisions behind choosing a mate. It treats partner search as the same kind of problem as food search, with signals guiding each choice.
arxiv-2604-00593: Takeuchi builds a geometric theory of cosmic structure from entropy-based curvature in Wasserstein space. The frame rests on optimal transport theory and transport geometry. Ricci curvature on the probability space is marked by the geodesic convexity of entropy, read as the response of distributions to optimal transport. He adds effective Ricci curvatures tied to Kullback-Leibler-type and Rényi-type entropy families, matching curvature-dimension rules. Pinning these values to finite scales with local and reference sets yields gauges usable on observed data.
arxiv-2604-00893: De Kinder and Caloz build a general theory of frequency shifts for light scattering at moving edges between dispersive media. From phase matching, they derive nonlinear shift rules showing dispersion reshapes the scattering picture, creating extra traveling waves with no match in plain media. For Drude, Lorentz, and double-Drude media, the theory shows how resonant dispersion, loss, and negative-index branches reorder scattering channels. It gives closed-form coefficients for the two-wave class.
arxiv-2604-01093: McCallum and colleagues present a reconstruction of the nearby line-of-sight Galactic magnetic field, combining a 3D electron-density map from dust-informed simulations with a Faraday rotation map. Their model evaluates rotation on the 3D grid and infers the field with a Gaussian-process prior whose power spectrum comes from the data. Where latitude exceeds 5 degrees, the field averages 1.63 microgauss, showing coherent patches with alternating sign plus structure near 100 parsecs. The field's 3D power spectrum slopes downward, and pulsar checks confirm the reconstruction.
arxiv-2604-01293: Song and Hosur solve exactly the quantum motion of a spinning Weyl fermion inside a finite cylinder. The setup probes rotation-driven axial currents in chiral matter. They recover Vilenkin's on-axis current density and show its cross-section average fades in a large system. The bulk response is thus purely a magnetization current. With spin-polarized edges, they also find sturdy chiral modes that pump axial charge under rotation, steady against temperature, Fermi level and Weyl speeds but tied to the mode count.
arxiv-2604-01593: Roy and colleagues offer a regression model for data gathered at set times but at shifting places. Their model handles links between readings plus variables that may be infinite-dimensional, with no fixed number of directions. Since the usual mixing-type dependence rule fails here, they use a weaker polynomially decaying moment contraction rule. They derive estimates for the mean and covariate functions and prove those estimates are consistent. A joint interval for the mean follows, backed by simulations and two studies.
arxiv-2604-01993: Kwon, Yoon and Hwang build SAFE, a verifier framework checking multi-hop reasoning step by step against evidence, instead of judging answers. Benchmarks reward models reaching right answers through faulty steps. SAFE splits reasoning into atomic evidence grounded units expressed as knowledge graph triples. At training time it verifies supervision under constraints, and at inference time a verifier checks each step, flags invalid reasoning and feeds corrections before errors spread. Across three multi hop benchmarks, accuracy rose by 8.8 points, showing stepwise verification beats post hoc judgment for evidence grounded reasoning.
arxiv-2604-02293: Ustyuzhanin proposes a covariate balanced stacked difference in differences method for settings where untreated trends run parallel only within groups. Matching or weighting fixes treated control balance within each stack, while corrective stacked weights recover the target aggregate effect. The logic extends from absorbing treatment to repeated treatments and episodes under finite memory. Tests on Trounstine and Acemoglu data show the method bridges stacked DID and design based panel matching.
arxiv-2604-02393: Maleknia and Sato give a moving picture of learning in multi layer nets, where vanishing gradients and overfitting are usually studied only at large scale. Training moves through plateau and near optimal regions, both shaped by saddle structures, before settling in that regime. Under suitable data that regime collapses to a single attractor modulo symmetry. For finite noisy datasets, the ideal optimum proves unreachable, and learning must end there.
arxiv-2604-02893: Nguyen-Truong, Balbay and Bayrak tackle visual explanation in geometry education as referring image segmentation: given a diagram and a description, produce a pixel mask for the named geometric element. Existing models trained on natural photos fail catastrophically on abstract diagrams. Their procedural engine generates over 200,000 synthetic geometry diagrams with pixel-perfect masks and varied referring expressions, and fine-tuned Florence-2 reaches 49 percent IoU against under 1 percent zero-shot.
arxiv-2604-02993: Moura and eight colleagues model globular cluster systems of 17 compact massive galaxies in Illustris TNG100, seeking links to massive relic galaxies that barely evolve over cosmic time. Clusters attach to stellar particles by age and local conditions, giving positions, motions, and chemistry. Combining assembly histories, size evolution, and traits such as in-situ versus ex-situ origin, metallicity, and spread, the team finds signs of early formation plus late accretion. The cluster mass fraction tracks host assembly better than the number fraction, and three galaxies emerge as relic analogs.
arxiv-2604-03093: Shim and colleagues work out which filament scales most shape a forming dark-matter halo inside the cosmic web. They find the tidal influence peaks when the smoothing scale is about two to three times the halo patch, with a formula tying it to peak rarity. By formation redshift, the scale around typical peaks follows a compact rule for survey and simulation teams picking scales.
arxiv-2604-03393: Kwok and colleagues present TABQAWORLD, a training-free framework for multi-turn table question answering that fixes representation errors from fixed text serialization. It switches dynamically between visual and textual table views for reliable readouts, and it plans trajectories using table metadata while compressing simple actions. Tests show about 5 percent accuracy gains over baselines and latency down about 33 percent against static settings.
arxiv-2604-03493: van Liemt and colleagues test whether large language models portray cultures the way native people see them. Diversity or factual checks alone do not capture that alignment. They build human-derived Cultural Importance Vectors from open surveys in nine countries. They then compare them with model-derived Cultural Representation Vectors for three frontier models. Some models skew Western, with alignment falling as countries sit farther from the US culturally. All models over-index on surface markers while missing deep social priorities.
arxiv-2604-03593: Molla and Goswami study a discrete-time quantum walk with a detector that is removed again and again after a span and put back at random spots. Two move rules are compared. Model 1 puts the detector back anywhere beyond its start point. Model 2 puts it back within a narrow window around its current spot. Both behave like a Semi Infinite Walk for long gaps between moves. For fast moves the models differ sharply, and the presence share ratio reaches a steady value for both.
arxiv-2604-03793: Mahesh Ramani studied how many queens are needed to dominate a three-dimensional n-by-n-by-n board. Each queen attacks along rows, columns, diagonals, and their 3D analogues. His stratified theorem counts, for corner, edge, face, and interior spots, how many inner-core cells a queen covers. Interior queens cover strictly more than boundary queens. Symmetry cuts and counting bounds then give a growth rate on the order of n squared, with exact values certified up to n equal to 6.
arxiv-2604-03893: Zeyu Wang and colleagues built FeynmanBench, a test set of over 2,000 tasks asking models to read Feynman diagrams in full. Each item pairs a diagram with short text and asks for vertex lists, propagator types, topology, momentum routing, and the full scattering amplitude. Nineteen leading multimodal models scored 70 to 95 percent on local spotting but fell to 13 to 17 percent on rebuilding topology, near zero on full derivation. The gap shows a deep weak spot in diagram-based science reasoning.
arxiv-2604-04193: Sarisht Wadhwa and team showed that parallel execution breaks many transaction fee mechanisms on modern blockchains. When parallelism affects fees, users can insert useless side trades just to cut fees, and schedulers can add useless sequential transactions to raise revenue. Execution contingency worsens these threats and adds two more: users may overpay for unused resources, and scheduler revenue falls when reserved slots go unused. The authors proved an impossibility result: parallelism and contingency force a trade-off between user and scheduler risk, and their mechanisms reach the trade-off boundaries.
arxiv-2604-04293: Spalas evaluates security for LDACS, the planned digital radio link between aircraft and control towers. A recent proposal secures its login step with physical unclonable functions, chip fingerprints that should be hard to copy. The paper shows three threats: advanced models can predict these fingerprints, quantum computers menace current cryptography, and aging makes the fingerprints unstable enough to knock the system offline. Together they open the door to impersonation attacks. Spalas instead proposes the established Public Key Infrastructure as the safer alternative.
arxiv-2604-04493: Li, Ma and Kang present SLaB, a framework splitting each linear layer weight into a sparse matrix, a low-rank matrix and a binary matrix. Model compression methods like pruning can help, but most fail to hold performance at high compression. SLaB needs no retraining and uses activation-aware pruning scores to guide the split. Tests on Llama models show state-of-the-art performance. Perplexity falls by up to 36 percent against existing methods at 50 percent compression, and accuracy rises by up to 8.98 percent on zero-shot tasks.
arxiv-2604-05193: Barooni and four colleagues use DFT to study the magnet ground state of LaCoO3 under strain. Strained LaCoO3 films show a magnet blocking state absent in bulk. They find high-spin and low-spin Co3+ ions: 2 by 2 columns of switching ions, split by planes of ions. Exchange gives magnet links via 90 degree paths and anti-magnet links via 180 degree paths, aided by empty holes. The 90 degree magnet links beat the 180 ones, locking the state.
arxiv-2604-05793: Ma, Wu, and Yan guard prompt privacy in language-model agent pipelines with BodhiPromptShield, a mediation layer that stops sensitive spans before they spread. Flagged spans turn into typed placeholders, abstractions, or secure tokens, restored only at approved boundaries. Leftover identifier leaks drop to 7.4 percent on one test set and under 2 percent on another, though human checks show meaning leaks persist.
arxiv-2604-05893: Berlea and twenty-three colleagues present a parametric simulation tool for pixel sensors driven purely by measurement input. The fast package avoids proprietary process details required by technology CAD tools, suiting large systems and high hit rates. Validation on the MALTA2 sensor plus periphery tweaks in the hit merger optimizes tracking and calorimetry ahead of the MALTA3 redesign.
arxiv-2604-06493: Li and Pilaftsis describe a new route to low-scale leptogenesis, the process behind the matter-antimatter imbalance. Heavy-neutrino mixing and sterile-neutrino oscillation, the usual routes, both demand nearly equal singlet neutrino masses to offset weak couplings. Their mechanism instead leans on resonant thermal lepton-flavour coherences at two-loop level, after extending the flavour-covariant Kadanoff-Baym formalism. It works for Dirac and Majorana singlets alike, needs no near-degeneracy, and allows heavy neutrino masses as low as a GeV.
arxiv-2604-06693: Baskaran, Pherwani, and Krishnan design Aegon, an audit layer for AI content licensing. Current standards tell AI systems the license terms, but none keep tamper-evident records proving those records were never rewritten. Aegon extends standard JWT tokens with content-specific licensing claims and logs transactions in a Merkle tree over an append-only ledger, so outside auditors can verify entries independently. Publishers check tokens at the edge without a broker, provenance events track content through AI transformation stages, and Android agents add hardware-attested receipts from StrongBox secure elements.
arxiv-2604-06793: Wang and four colleagues judge repository documentation by whether it lets models do the work. Existing benchmarks score documentation or lean on LLM-as-a-judge with vague criteria and thin repository knowledge. SWD-Bench instead tests if a model can understand and implement features from the documentation alone, through detection, localization, and completion questions. Built from 4,170 mined pull requests with repository context, it exposes limits in current documentation methods and shows source code adding complementary value. Documentation from the best method lifts SWE-Agent issue solving by 20 percent.
arxiv-2604-07493: Hod and five colleagues build a safe pipeline for tracking disease spread on sensitive contact networks. Contact data can expose sexual relationships or drug use, so summaries are computed under node-level differential privacy. A statistical network model fitted to those summaries makes synthetic networks for agent-based spread simulation. Tests on ARTNet sexual-network data show privacy noise is small beside sampling and model error, so curators can share useful epidemic insights while protecting people.
arxiv-2604-07793: Arushi and Kumar develop a higher-order finite element method for the multidimensional fragmentation equation, which models how particles break apart. To their knowledge, theirs is the first rigorous conforming finite element framework for high-order spatial approximation of such models. The scheme is set variationally, and its stability and convergence follow from detailed analysis. An L2 projection yields optimal-order spatial error estimates under suitable regularity assumptions. Time stepping uses a second-order backward differentiation formula, giving a fully discrete scheme with second-order convergence in time.
arxiv-2604-07993: Bai and 17 colleagues present HEX, a state-centric framework for coordinated whole-body manipulation by full-sized bipedal humanoid robots. Most vision-language-action models treat body parts largely independently, making high-degree-of-freedom robot control unstable. HEX introduces a body-aligned universal state representation for learning across varied robot bodies. A mixture-of-experts unified proprioceptive predictor models whole-body coordination and motion dynamics over time from large multi-body trajectory data. Lightweight history tokens sum up past observations, avoiding repeated encoding of old images during inference.
arxiv-2604-08093: Bekaert and Pannier develop a gauge theory of 2D higher-spin gravity with vanishing cosmological constant using a BF formulation of dilaton gravity. The formulation defines gauge theories of the Poincaré or Maxwell algebras and several higher-spin generalizations, finite and infinite dimensional. The spectrum of higher-spin gravity based on the extended infinite-dimensional algebra contains infinite scalar degrees of freedom with a continuum of rising mass, corresponding to the twisted-adjoint representation. The paper comments on including scalar-field backreaction on gravity in formal equations of motion.
arxiv-2604-08293: De Luca and four colleagues present CIAO, a structured process that auto-generates system-level documentation straight from GitHub repositories with Large Language Models. Software architecture documentation matters for comprehension, yet it is often missing or incomplete. While recent LLM-based techniques can create documentation from code, they usually cover local artifacts, not coherent system-level descriptions. CIAO defines an LLM-based workflow taking a repository as input and producing system-level documentation from a template based on ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010, SEI Views and Beyond, and the C4 model.
arxiv-2604-08493: Perna and Domènech examine how an unusual reheat era shapes waves born from scalar ripples, with early non Gaussianity. Values for the cosmic fluid and its sound speed leave marks that third generation detectors like LISA could spot, while reheat shifts can suppress or boost the signal. A Fisher check across amplitudes and central frequencies gauges how detectable the signal remains under varied reheat cases.
arxiv-2604-08693: Pradhan, Prihar, and Ottmar learn problem free codes of whole algebraic solution paths to capture student strategies. Step change vectors from differences between one solution state and the next feed SimCSE contrastive learning, placing similar paths near each other and separating different strategies. Tests on action sorting, efficiency tests, and sequence replay show the codes hold real strategy information, with uniqueness, diversity, and conformity scores tracking learning results.
arxiv-2604-08793: Ghosh and Bassler present Qbg, a new score for finding layered groups in two sided networks. A tuning knob scans structure across scales, using limit effects to reveal layers without flattening the network or breaking its two sided shape. Tests on a layered fake benchmark and two real networks recover known mid scale structure plus finer layered detail beyond standard two sided methods.
arxiv-2604-08893: Suraki presents ADRUwAMS, a tuning dual skip U-Net with focus gates and multi size spatial focus for glioma cutting. Gliomas demand early finding, yet tumor place and size make split from healthy tissue hard, and deep learning offers a reliable path. Dual tuning skip paths capture high level meaning detail and fine low level detail, focus gates weight input signals, and multi size spatial focus maps hold the most key tumor information. Trained 200 epochs on BraTS 2019 and 2020, it reaches a dice score of 0.9229 for the whole tumor.
arxiv-2604-09093: Avraham-Re'em and Björklund study stationary actions of locally compact groups through Radon-Nikodym cocycles. Extending Furstenberg-Glasner to noncompact locally compact groups, they show every stationary action is conservative and therefore never of type one. The paper also proves a compact model theorem built on it. By contrast, a random walk on the real affine group has a Poisson boundary failing Kaimanovich's SAT* property. Its Poisson kernel grows unbounded near identity. Hence Harnack's inequality fails for positive harmonic functions, and no continuous-kernel model exists for this boundary.
arxiv-2604-09193: Amisi, Gómez-Ortiz, Bousquet, and Ghosez report a hidden ground state of silver niobate, a perovskite oxide long classed as antiferroelectric. Calculations reveal a ferroelectric phase with R3 symmetry that sits lowest in energy, nearly tied with earlier proposed structures. The phase is chiral, its handedness arising from coupling between electric polarization and oxygen octahedra rotations, with incomplete cancellation of local chiral motifs. That chirality yields strong natural optical activity much like quartz, though slow kinetics may explain why experiments missed it.
arxiv-2604-09393: Rahaman, Kalita, and Pramanik model miscible viscous fingering of a finite slice with a high-order compact method. Viscous fingering arises in uniform porous media, with flow under Darcy's law and solute transport by flow-diffusion. Thickness depends on solute strength, making contrast between pushing fluid and finite sample. Three boundary types are tested: cyclic, sealed with no flux, and open with no diffusive flux. Onset and early conduct prove free of boundary type, but long-time mixing depends on it, with open boundaries raising solute mass and boosting fingering.
arxiv-2604-09493: Solanki, Praharaj, Deepti Gupta, and Maanak Gupta present a policy-aware language model lookup plan for battlefield missions. Large language models offer a handy front end for intent-driven control of self-run systems. Direct use in mission-critical war-zone settings raises safety and policy concerns. Their plan combines a lookup module grounding choices in policies and live data with a hosted planning model and a Judge model checking commands. Built in a mock setting using RoboDK, Gemma-2B hit the best score at about 4 seconds and 100 percent success.
arxiv-2604-09693: Li and four colleagues introduce TaFall, a balance-informed fall detector using privacy-preserving thermal sensing for private indoor settings. Radio-frequency approaches lean on coarse motion cues. TaFall models falls as balance degradation. Appearance-motion fusion reconstructs pose from low-resolution thermal maps. Balance-aware learning and pose-bridged pretraining add robustness. On over 3,000 instances from 35 participants, detection reaches about 98 percent with under 1 percent false alarms. A 27-day deployment across four homes shows near-zero false alarms. A bathroom pilot confirms moisture and thermal robustness.
arxiv-2604-09793: He-Yueya and seven co-authors introduce insight anticipation: predicting a downstream paper's core insight from its parent papers. They build GiantsBench, 17,000 examples across eight domains pairing parent sets with downstream insights. A language-model judge scores generated insights against ground truth, correlating with expert ratings. The team trains GIANTS-4B with reinforcement learning on these scores. Despite its smaller open-source build, GIANTS-4B beats proprietary baselines, generalizes to unseen domains, and gains 34 percent over gemini-3-pro. Human judges find its insights clearer than the base model's.
arxiv-2604-10093: Ruotolo and nine colleagues introduce CHESSY, an open-source framework linking SystemC virtual platforms to FPGA emulation for early prototyping of cyber-physical systems. The FPGA runs the main digital subsystems while a wrapper keeps timing and communication in step with simulated peripherals over JTAG. A RISC-V system-on-chip example from biosignal processing runs up to 2500 times faster than register-transfer-level simulation, while staying within twice the time of pure FPGA emulation.
arxiv-2604-10493: Dihan and Khan give code agents step by step grades from process reward models. Long repository jobs need steady choices across edits, file hunts, and test runs. Their SWE-Shepherd frame trains a light PRM reward model on past SWE-Bench runs. At run time, the model scores each candidate move and steers toward richer picks. Tests on SWE-Bench Verified show leaner talks and better moves, though reward fit still lags final wins.
arxiv-2604-10693: Sun and five colleagues propose FACT-E, a causality-based check on chain-of-thought reasoning in language models. Models often write sound-looking explanations that hide steps that do not truly follow, and self-checks tend to endorse them anyway. FACT-E uses small controlled changes to separate real step links from bias-driven noise, yielding steadier faithfulness scores. Paired with answer checks, it picks paths faithful inside and backing the right answer. Tests on GSM8K, MATH, and CommonsenseQA show better path picks and stronger teaching examples.
arxiv-2604-11193: Wang, Huang, Wang, and Yin build TRACE, a framework for answering questions that need several hops across a knowledge graph. It turns evolving reasoning paths into plain-language narratives to keep meaning continuous, and distills past explorations into reusable priors that guide which relation to follow next. A dual-feedback reranking step blends both signals, and tests on several benchmarks beat leading baselines.
arxiv-2604-11293: Ge and six colleagues revisit GeV gamma-ray emission from the shell-type supernova remnant Vela Jr using 15 years of Fermi-LAT data. The emission shape best matches a masked H.E.S.S. shell template, implying the embedded pulsar wind nebula adds little GeV flux. The spectrum follows a hard power law with index 1.77 that joins smoothly to the TeV spectrum. A hybrid lepton-hadron model fits the full multi-wavelength data better than a pure leptonic model, supporting a mixed origin.
arxiv-2604-11393: Girard and Lapenta estimate average marginal effects in partly linear instrumental regressions with a one-parameter kernel method. They prove the estimator works in large samples and is normal in the limit. The limit variance has a hard analytic form, so they use a bootstrap for inference and prove it valid. Simulations show good small-sample results, and three real-data uses yield meaningful economic results. The work is easy to run and works well in practice.
arxiv-2604-11493: Vulić and three colleagues observe discrete 1D solitons in a photonic lattice induced in rubidium vapor. Two coupling laser fields crossing at an angle create a modulated refractive index. A probe beam focused into a lattice site first shows discrete diffraction. Raising probe intensity yields discrete solitons from the balance of discrete diffraction and self-focusing in the nonlinear atomic matter. Simulations with optical Bloch equations for a multilevel Lambda system support the results. Controllable gain and loss in atomic vapors make the platform promising for non-Hermitian dynamics.
arxiv-2604-11593: Jamshed and six colleagues survey Integrated Sensing and Communication for non-terrestrial networks in 6G. Non-terrestrial networks aim for smart, always-on links, but Doppler shifts, interference, and delay block smooth links with terrestrial networks. Joining sensing and communication in one setup, ISAC can ease those blocks and add new uses, though uptake needs new designs and rules. The piece covers design rules, use cases, standardization hurdles, and performance trade-offs, and ends with a case study and next steps.
arxiv-2604-11993: Sohoni and nine colleagues use correlated-photon illumination to boost object recognition in ultra-low-light, noisy imaging. Signal photons match up in space while noise clicks do not. Earlier work used that fact to rebuild images; here the goal is inference instead. Their CAT method jointly tunes a trainable photon source and a Transformer backend, using at most 100 shots. Accuracy rises by up to 15 points over standard uncorrelated light, and beats untrained correlated light too.
arxiv-2604-12493: Michael Hanna and Emmanuel Ameisen study latent planning in large language models. Latent planning means inner plans that shape output without being spoken aloud. The team tests the Qwen-3 family, from 0.6 billion to 14 billion parameters. Planning skill grows with model size. Planning models hold features for a planned word, like accountant, that steer earlier words. Even mid-size models show early planning mechanisms. On rhyming couplets, models often pick a rhyme early but rarely plan far ahead. Steering toward planned words can elicit more planning as size grows.
arxiv-2604-12893: Maria Duque-Gijon and eight colleagues build a laser that fires like a neuron. Neuromorphic photonics needs small scalable light sources that mimic neural signals. Their single-stack VCSEL shows negative differential resistance, as in memristive devices. That behavior yields refractoriness and integrate-and-fire dynamics. The device works as an optical spiking neuron doing coincidence detection and exclusive OR logic. An array of such lasers could classify patterns. The laser suits sensing and computing, with low cost and easy integration.
arxiv-2604-13093: Wu designs a finite Lieb-lattice quantum circuit from spin-1/2 qubits and triplet couplers, a layout built from molecules carrying multiple radicals. Using tensor-network methods, he computes entanglement entropy, reduced density matrices, and spin-spin correlations while varying anisotropy and field strength. The study reveals rich entanglement patterns, quantum phase transitions, and tunable spin coherence, giving a base for molecule-based quantum circuits.
arxiv-2604-13693: Zeng and three colleagues debug slow WebAssembly runtimes with WarpL, a mutation-based method that pinpoints the exact faulty instruction sequences. Most runtime slowdowns come from poor compilation, which tools built for app-level waste handle badly. WarpL builds a functionally similar mutant where the slowdown vanishes. It then compares machine code between the original and the mutant to isolate the culprit instructions. On 12 real issues across three runtimes, it finds the exact cause in 10, including six previously unknown issues in Wasmtime.
arxiv-2604-13793: Mahdi and three colleagues generate first-person video from a synced third-person view. The jump between views breaks standard video models. Their Syn2Seq-Forcing method interpolates between source and target videos into a single continuous signal. That reframes exo-to-ego generation as sequential signal modeling for diffusion forcing transformers. Interpolating only the videos, without pose interpolation, already brings large gains. The same formulation also unifies ego-to-exo generation in one continuous sequence model.
arxiv-2604-13993: Lilienthal, Mukherjee, and Horawalavithana ask whether rewards for physical reasoning in vision-language models must come from outside or can come from the model itself. Outside rewards drive most accuracy gains, while an internal attention-based reward needs no labels and sharpens spatial-relation reasoning. Adding the internal reward to format and accuracy rewards lifts Molmo 2 accuracy at no extra annotation cost and generalizes to new tasks.
arxiv-2604-14093: Zhang, Men'shchikov, and Li measure the filament linear density function across seven nearby molecular clouds spanning 140 to 920 parsecs. The slope shows no trend with spatial scale, and the combined slope of about 1.4 matches the classic Salpeter slope in every cloud despite wide variation in supercritical-filament fractions. The match hints at a physical link between filamentary cloud structure and the stellar initial mass function.
arxiv-2604-14293: Prokof'ev and three colleagues challenge the belief that Migdal-Eliashberg Fermi liquids stay stable until the dressed phonon softens. In the Holstein model across wide fillings in three and two dimensions, a polaronic or bipolaronic state appears before phonon softening. At small filling in three dimensions this happens already at weak coupling. Upon raising coupling, the state emerges through a mixed pseudogap state where some fermions keep Fermi-liquid behavior yet Luttinger's theorem fails. At larger couplings the density of states gradually takes its atomic-limit form.
arxiv-2604-14693: König and 22 colleagues used the 2023/24 NICER watch on the black-hole binary Swift J1727.8-1613, bright at seven times the Crab, to trace its accretion disk through nearly every outburst state. Fitting the disk spectrum with a temperature-dependent color correction, they found the inner disk edge moved by a factor of a few between hard and soft states. They tentatively spot truncation setting in just after the soft state ends, with the luminous hard state more truncated than the dim one.
arxiv-2604-15093: Cheng and colleagues open up mobile-agent training with OpenMobile, a framework that writes its own tasks and trajectories. A synthesis pipeline explores phone environments, builds a shared memory of them, and turns it into varied, grounded instructions. Rollouts alternate learner and expert models to capture error-recovery steps that plain imitation misses. Fine-tuned models reach 64.7 percent on AndroidWorld, far ahead of prior open-data methods, and the team releases data and code.
arxiv-2604-15193: Hauck defines and studies the rational analytic syntomification of a partially proper rigid-analytic variety over the p-adic numbers. He proves Poincaré duality and a first-Chern-class theory for the new cohomology. Vector bundles on the syntomification match the de Rham bundles tied to the Fargues-Fontaine curve. Several classical comparison results in p-adic Hodge theory follow, with analogues over the complex p-adics.
arxiv-2604-15393: Jeong and three colleagues cast sequential quantum state discrimination as a partially observable Markov decision process with a static hidden state. The framing subsumes minimum-error discrimination as its one-step special case. Grid splitting of the belief simplex plus a finite measurement library yields tight error bounds and complexity studies for offline planning and online execution, with binary and trine cases showing the structure.
arxiv-2604-16093: Patra and 16 colleagues present TDE 2025abcr, the second optical off-nuclear tidal disruption event about 9 kpc from its host nucleus. Hydrogen and helium lines confirm TDE-H-He class. Modeling implies a black hole of a million to ten million solar masses, far smaller than the nucleus one. Velocity shifts from minus 500 to plus 1000 km/s point to an evolving reprocessing layer. Its infrared spectrum runs shallower than the Rayleigh-Jeans slope, ruling out dust. Free-free emission or a stellar cluster remain possible, suggesting a stripped satellite remnant.
arxiv-2604-16193: Ferres and Gauvin correct socioeconomic bias in mobility estimates drawn from mobile-phone call records in Santiago, Chile. Because one carrier's users skew by social group, simple averages get distorted. One such average is travel radius. Fitting a Bayesian multilevel model by socioeconomic status, gender, and place, then reweighting to census demographics, cuts the naive average radius estimate by about 17 percent. Even a geography-only version captures much of the bias.
arxiv-2604-16393: Wu, Li, Stolee and Xu studied how programmers work with AI help, looking beyond prompts and edits to intentions and feelings. In a study, 76 developers split into AI-assisted and unaided groups completed programming tasks and labelled their intentions, actions and emotions from screen recordings. The team distilled the results into S-IASE, a model spanning intention, action, supporting tool and emotion. AI-assisted developers stayed more focused on creating and checking code, and steadier emotionally, though some reported guilt or self-doubt about relying on help.
arxiv-2604-16493: Hou and colleagues present NL2SQLBench, a modular framework for testing language-model systems that turn plain questions into SQL. It splits such systems into three modules, schema choice, candidate generation and query revision, and scores each with fine-grained metrics. Testing ten open methods on two datasets with two language models exposed large gaps. Accuracy still needs work, and heavy compute costs block real-world use. The study also faults benchmarks for inaccurate gold SQL and weak rules, setting a fairer reference for future work.
arxiv-2604-16693: Gordon builds a trace framework for self-similar Casimir systems. Quantum fields meet shapes in regimes, from spectra to Casimir setups and cavities. Thermal equations and asymptotics are known, but vacuum treatments mix strict bounds with models. He separates regimes, joining the trace of radiation with a cold vacuum trace for flat shapes. Where a Casimir factor governs, the stress tensor yields a trace tied to its log running. He separates that from trace anomalies on fractal edges. Finite prefractal cases set needs for a theory tests can check.
arxiv-2604-16793: Vaheb, Fabbro and Draper evaluate deep-learning denoising methods trainable without clean ground-truth images for astronomy. Low photon counts force long post-processing, including dirt removal and denoising. Noise2Noise, Stein's Unbiased Risk Estimator and blind-spot methods are compared on synthetic data and real Hubble and Canada-France-Hawaii observations. Object-detection metrics, image metrics and pixel-distribution diagnostics judge performance. The methods improve faint-source detectability over noisy images, with encouraging Hubble gains after domain-consistent initialization but more limited transfer to Canada-France-Hawaii data.
arxiv-2604-16893: Qin and colleagues present EasyVideoR1, a full fast reinforcement learning framework for training vision-language models on video understanding. Spreading checked-reward reward learning to video is largely new, hindered by task range, decoding cost and touchy hyperparameters. Offline preprocessing with tensor caching kills repeat video reading, yielding one point four seven times throughput gain. A task-aware reward system covers 11 video and image problem types, and joint training uses alone settable pixel budgets. Async evaluation covers 22 mainstream video benchmarks, with redone results closely aligned with formal given scores.
arxiv-2604-17293: Ren and seven colleagues present UA-Bench, a benchmark of over 3,500 questions from six knowledge and thought sets for testing doubt tagging. Prior work treats refusal as generic, failing to split input fog (data doubt) from skill limits (model doubt), curbing follow-ups or tool-use choices. Testing 18 models shows even top models struggle to tell data doubt from model doubt, and high answer scores do not imply strong tagging. Lightweight data mixing and reward learning lift tagging on two Qwen3 models in thinking mode while keeping answer scores.
arxiv-2604-17693: Deshmukh and three colleagues propose COSAC, a critic-free policy gradient method, one per agent, for sequential teams. Critic methods scale poorly, while critic-free options add noise or calls. COSAC fits an additive per-agent split of team reward by one ridge regression, and computes counterfactual advantages from fictitious continuations. Its Sequential Aristocrat Utility carries bounds controlled as teams grow. On bandits up to 16 agents, COSAC attains the lowest advantage error and low regret, and on an ARC task with four agents, it converges faster than baselines.
arxiv-2604-17893: Uchida and seven colleagues use large language models to generate dynamic, context-rich questions for learning by teaching. Such questions replace rigid templates that are costly to build. In an English vocabulary study, learners who explained concepts through the system retained more than those using traditional methods. The edge held when tested at three and seven days, in a small group of ten participants. The team also links certain learner traits to stronger gains, pointing toward tailored versions of the approach.
arxiv-2604-17993: Bigoni and two colleagues show that transverse loads on an elastic rod, long assumed harmless, can act like axial loads. Two equal opposite loads across the rod give zero net force, yet three rod models reveal the same deformation as an axial load. In a generalized Euler elastica the transverse load joins the axial load, causing buckling under compression. The buckling threshold mirrors the Euler axial form and falls to zero as rod inertia vanishes, so instability persists even for vanishing thickness, as simulations and experiments confirm.
arxiv-2604-18093: Hu, Gao, Wu, and Ren examine two flat ferroelectric materials, Tl2S and SnS. Electric polarization in these materials can steer a flow of orbital angular momentum. Polarization pointing within the plane couples strongly to higher-order topology. It can flip the orbital Hall plateau inside the energy gap on demand, pointing toward electrically controlled orbitronic devices.
arxiv-2604-18593: Zaliva and six colleagues present HELIX, a code-generation system with proofs of correctness for cyber-physical control problems, aimed at LLVM code. It starts from a high-level math statement of the problem, then applies algebra steps through mid-level languages to reach fast code for the target machine. Each step keeps the meaning intact, as shown by proofs built in Coq, and a robot control case runs the whole chain end to end.
arxiv-2604-18693: Bhattacherjee and four colleagues propose DELIGHT-SHIELD, a detector plan for finding long-lived particles beyond the Standard Model at a future 100 TeV collider. In place of inner tracking, a layered shield sits ahead of tracking volumes downstream. The shield cuts ordinary hadronic and electromagnetic backgrounds by as much as seven orders of magnitude on paper, and full runs back a level low enough to work with. Test cases reach branching ratios as low as about one in a billion.
arxiv-2604-18993: Hu and eight colleagues present AutoAWG, a controllable weather video generation framework for autonomous driving. Real adverse weather video is scarce, and past methods trade visual quality against annotation reuse. AutoAWG fuses multiple controls guided by scene semantics, balancing weather style with faithful preservation of safety targets. Vanishing point synthesis builds training sequences from still images, and masked training steadies long horizon generation. On nuScenes validation, AutoAWG beats prior methods: FID falls 50 percent and FVD about 16 percent without first-frame conditioning, with further gains under it.
arxiv-2604-19193: Zhang and eleven colleagues ask how far video models are from true multimodal thought, introducing CLVG-Bench for zero-shot thought via Context Learning in Video Generation. The benchmark holds over 1,000 metadata in 6 categories and 47 subcategories. An Adaptive Video Evaluator matches expert judgment using few annotations and gives clear feedback. Top models like Seedance 2.0 handle some subtasks but fall short on grounded and interactive generation, with success under 25 percent and about 0 percent, showing multimodal thought and physical grounding as limits.
arxiv-2604-19493: Çadırcı and Ünal introduce a nonparametric goodness-of-fit test for high-dimensional generalized Gaussian distributions. The test uses nearest-neighbor graph topology and is affine-invariant. Classical tests lean on covariance inversion or density estimation. Those tools falter when dimension rivals or exceeds sample size. After robust standardization, the new procedure builds a reference sample and measures the cross-sample pattern on the combined graph. The method needs no prior guess about the shape of the data.
arxiv-2604-19593: Timpuriu, Mihaela-Claudia Cercel, and Dumitru-Clementin Cercel introduce RoLegalGEC, a legal-domain grammar correction dataset for Romanian. Clear and correct text matters greatly in legal papers. A tool for lawyers must grasp errors in a legal context and train on realistic legal data. Data annotated by hand for such training is scarce for Romanian, let alone for a niche domain. Synthetic generation of parallel data is the most common workaround, but it demands a structured grasp of the grammar.
arxiv-2604-19693: Centorrino and Parmeter review recent efforts to merge causal inference tools with the stochastic frontier model used to study productivity and efficiency. Causal tools such as instrumental variables, difference-in-differences, and regression discontinuity are standard across the social sciences. Yet their use has lagged in frontier studies because the model's error component resists a causal reading. The review surveys modeling approaches and empirical issues likely to matter for applied researchers, showing how the model fits within a causal frame.
arxiv-2604-19893: Van Wijk and five colleagues extend backup control barrier functions to output feedback, where controllers see only an estimate of the true state. Backup barrier methods keep bounded-input systems safe by forecasting the flow under a prescribed controller, but state estimates blur that forecast. Their technique wraps the estimated flow in an uncertainty envelope, proving envelope safety guarantees true-state safety. A feasible safe control always exists under this scheme, even with input limits and state uncertainty.
arxiv-2604-19993: Zhang and three colleagues enable uncertainty estimates for complex-valued neural networks, which handle complex numbers but could not gauge confidence. Their dropout-based Bayesian networks, BayesCVNNs, are the first, and an automated search tunes real and imaginary parts through layer and part mixing. A generator builds custom FPGA accelerators from optimized blocks, and the best designs beat hand-built models at lower hardware cost. They run about four and a half times and thirteen times faster than GPU versions, and use under 10 percent of GPU power.
